2026 MLB playoff bracket: Schedule, scores as Guardians force Game 5 vs. White Sox in ALDS
Three teams have clinched their spots in the LCS round, while the Guardians have forced a decisive Game 5 against the White Sox
By
Kate Feldman
Oct 9, 2026
at
11:36 am ET
2 min read
Add CBS Sports on Google
Adam Eargle, CBS Sports Design
Just five teams remain in the 2026 MLB playoff field. The Dodgers, Rays and Brewers all advanced to the LCS round on Wednesday night, knocking the Braves, Yankees and Padres out, respectively. The two-time reigning champion Dodgers will face the Brewers in the NLCS for the second straight year, while the Rays await the Guardians-White Sox winner in the ALCS.
Guardians vs. White Sox is the only LDS series still going, and Cleveland kept its season alive with a 9-5 road win in Game 4. Chicago is trying to reach the ALCS for the first time since winning the World Series in 2005. To do so, it will have to win Game 5 in Cleveland on Saturday night.
The Astros, Red Sox, Cubs and Phillies were already knocked out in the best-of-three Wild Card Series last week.
Below is a look at the full 2026  MLB playoff bracket and the playoff schedule.

The Atlanta Dream and the Golden State Valkyries will square off in the 2026 WNBA Finals. The Dream and Valkyries both completed semifinal sweeps on Friday night. Atlanta knocked out the New York Liberty, while Golden State ousted the reigning champion Las Vegas Aces. The 2026 WNBA Finals are set to begin on Oct. 17.
Neither the Dream nor the Valkyries has ever won a WNBA championship. It's Atlanta's first Finals appearance since 2013. It's the first for the Valkyries, who are just in their second season as a franchise after debuting as an expansion team in 2025.

The 2026 WNBA season has been groundbreaking, on and off the court. It launched on the heels of a contentious and extended labor battle that resulted in a historic raise for the players (the salary cap increased from $1.5 million in 2025 to $7 million in 2026), and in return, the players raised the bar on a weekly basis. We've got four weeks of football under our belts, which should mean we are starting to feel more certain about player roles and performance. That would probably be more true if we didn't lose a handful of stars to injury seemingly every week. Still, I feel confident saying we know a lot more now than we did a month ago. This newfound knowledge comes just in time for the first byes of the season. Normally, a two-team bye week is worthy of a yawn, but in Week 5, we'll be missing two top 12 quarterbacks, two top 12 running backs, a top 12 receiver, and a top 12 tight end. In other words, we've got work to do.
One thing I hope to avoid as I do this weekly is calling a guy a faller one week and a riser the next week. But we had a lot of guys that we all but gave up on after three bad weeks who finally popped. At the very least, we have to address some of those, starting with Malik Nabers. We also have some big matchup shifts, which always impact the weekly projections.
Prominent players, we had projected last week that we are not projecting to play in Week 5 as of Monday evening:
Lamar Jackson, Ja'Marr Chase, Saquon Barkley, Ladd McConkey, DJ, Moore, Kyle Monangai, Mack Hollins, Marcus Mariota
At the bottom of this article are my Week 5 projections for quarterback, running back, wide receiver, and tight end. They will be updated throughout the week as we get more information.
Risers
Jared Goff, QB, Lions
The first thing that is going to stand out to you is that Jared Goff is QB1 for Week 5. I'm not sure it should be that big of a surprise. He is QB5 on a per-game basis for the season, and he's facing a Cardinals defense that has given up the fourth-most fantasy points to opposing defenses. I could make the argument that they have been the worst pass defense in the league, but if they haven't, it may be Goff's Lions. Goff's Lions have an implied total of 29, which is both the biggest number on the weekend and slightly below their season average. It also helps Goff's case that Josh Allen is on the road against the Rams without DJ Moore.
Drake Maye, QB, Patriots
Maye is the first of the Week 4 rebounds who also rebound in my projections. His Patriots are 3.5-point favorites at home against the Raiders, and I mostly buy that Maye and the Patriots' pass game found something last week. He's not in the QB1 discussion like we thought he might be this system, but he does project as a QB1, and I would start him over most, if not all, of the streaming options. Maye ranks second behind only Lamar Jackson in quarterback rushing yards this season.
Will Shipley, RB, Eagles
As of Monday night, we aren't projecting Saquon Barkley or Tank Bigsby to play for the Eagles in Week 5. That makes Shipley one of the biggest risers of the week, as I project him for 18 Fantasy points against Jacksonville. This isn't a good matchup, and the Eagles aren't currently a good offense, but any time a running back projects for this much work, he is going to be a top-30 running back. I would expect Shipley to score around eight Fantasy points without a touchdown, and if he scores, he'll be an RB2. He should be one of the most popular names on the waiver wire.
RJ Harvey, RB, Broncos
Harvey saw 10 targets in Week 4, which certainly moved his projection needle, even if we don't expect a repeat performance. The Broncos offense looks a little broken right now and Harvey has been more efficient running the ball than J.K. Dobbins. With Jonah Coleman on Injured Reserve, we expect Harvey's rush share to increase and he will probably be top three on the team in target share as well. He's a very good PPR flex this week against the Chargers.
Ollie Gordon, RB, Dolphins
It was a wild week of speculation about the Dolphins running backs, but now we have some results. Gordon played 59.5% of the offensive snaps compared to Jaylen Wright's 29.7%. There was a similar split in rush share and surprisingly, Gordon also earned more targets. View him as a high-end flex who can be used as a low-end RB2 in a pinch. This is still a terrible offensive environment, but at least now we know who the lead back is.
Malik Nabers, WR, Giants
Nabers is the second guy who was a faller last week but rebounds as a riser in Week 5 after he broke out with six catches for 112 yards and a touchdown. I moved Nabers inside of my top 30 in this week's projections in what should be another good matchup. I may be a bit slower to move Nabers back into the top 20 because Jameis Winston still made a lot of bad throws against a bad defense and Isaiah Likely still dominated targets. Still, I suspect most people will feel comfortable starting Nabers in Week 5.
Carnell Tate, WR, Titans
Tate had a monster Week 4 and now ranks 4th amongst all receivers with a 29.6% target share. He's also in the top 10 for first-read share. Cam Ward is making an effort to get his rookie receiver more involved and the results are promising. This is still a bad offense, but they did look slightly more competent against the Ravens in Week 4. Week 5 brings a bad matchup against the Texans, we think. The Texans have not played up to their reputation this season. I would start Tate as a low-end RW5 in Week 5.

The Arizona Cardinals are finalizing a deal to  trade wide receiver Marvin Harrison Jr., informing the former first-round pick of their decision ahead of Sunday's game against the Detroit Lions, ESPN reports. Arizona desires a second-round pick or better in exchange for the former Ohio State star, according to Tom Pelissero.
Details of the trade are reportedly still being finalized, but Harrison is inactive for Sunday's game. The subject of recent trade speculation, Harrison has drawn interest from the Indianapolis Colts, among others, who are looking for a weapon in the passing game. However, longtime Colts reporter Mike Chappell reported Saturday that the Colts are not in the Harrison sweepstakes after initially doing their due diligence.
The Houston Texans are among the teams who have been in contact with Arizona about Harrison Jr., Matt Zenitz of CBS Sports confirms.
General manager Monti Ossenfort publicly maintained that Harrison remains part of the franchise's plans, but that appears moot after Sunday's reported deal. Harrison hasn't given the Cardinals reasons to feature him this season, with drops and productivity concerns.
A fresh start might eventually benefit everyone involved.
The ex-Ohio State standout who entered the NFL in 2024 as the franchise's fourth-overall pick hasn't been as impactful as expected, given his meteoric rise ahead of that offseason's draft.
Harrison registered 608 yards in 12 games last season, and through four games in 2026, only five catches for 85 yards. Over 16 starts as a rookie, Harrison recorded 62 receptions for 885 yards and eight touchdowns before his production dwindled during his second campaign, part of that due to a concussion suffered last season.
What Harrison brings to new team
A change of scenery could benefit Harrison, a 24-year-old talent whose size and body control impact the game when consistently targeted. His appeal is obvious — an athlete with his catch radius is covered in short-yardage situations and goal-to-go opportunities.
While he hasn't been the field-stretcher most assumed he would be early at the next level, perhaps Harrison's new team unlocks a certain level of comfort in a different scheme.
Cardinals first-year offensive coordinator Nathaniel Hackett seemed uninterested in moving Harrison around and manufacturing touches for a player the franchise was paying $35.3 million to during his four-year rookie deal. The plan was for Harrison to be Arizona's new No. 1 when drafted, but that never panned out, and his new landing spot won't have to tag him with that high an expectation level.
The bet is straightforward for the team that signs Harrison — get the most of his proven ability by providing a stable scheme around him that gets him more involved with the offense.
A player who was a two-time All-American with the Buckeyes and earned Biletnikoff honors as a junior in 2023 as the Big Ten's Offensive Player of the Year hasn't forgotten how to play football. Instead, he was never the right fit for a franchise that refused to mold its offense around his abilities.

No. 20 Iowa faced the unenviable task of traveling two times zones for Friday night's game at Washington on short rest after a physically taxing Week 5 loss to Ohio State. Further complicating matters for the Hawkeyes was a shoulder injury that kept starting quarterback Hank Brown out.
But with backup Jeremy Hecklinski slinging the rock, Iowa jumped out to an early four-touchdown lead and stunned the Huskies 41-24. In the process, the Hawkeyes reinserted themselves into the College Football Playoff hunt. At 5-1 and 2-1 in the Big Ten, Iowa is entering the second half of its schedule with a realistic path to a 10-2 record or even 11-1 if it runs the table.
A 10-2 Iowa team would have roughly a 60% chance of reaching the College Football Playoff, according to the CBS Sports College Football Forecaster.
Big Ten Power Rankings: The league's old West Division demands respect entering Week 6
Robby Kalland
The Hawkeyes are one of the strongest Power Four programs to have never made a CFP appearance. While the path ahead isn't necessarily easy, it's notable for what it doesn't include. There is no Indiana or Oregon on the docket. In fact, not a single team ranked in the AP Top 25 entering Week 6 action remains on Iowa's slate.
Kamari Moulton takes it 56 yards up the middle to the HOUSE for @HawkeyeFootball 💨 pic.twitter.com/JQnyPyPVXE— FOX College Football (@CFBONFOX) October 10, 2026
With Ohio State in the rearview mirror and Iowa's lone West Coast trip in the books as a resounding victory, Hawkeyes fans can enter a bye week with honest belief in their team's playoff potential.
Big Ten West lays ahead
The Big Ten dissolved its divisional structure after the 2023 season as it welcomed four former Pac-12 programs to the fold amid an expansion from 14 to 18 teams. But for those who remember the pre-realignment life, the best way to explain Iowa's remaining schedule is that it's literally the old Big Ten West. The CBS Sports College Football Forecaster gives the Hawkeyes between a 44% and 79% chance of winning every remaining game on their schedule.
Oct. 24 at Minnesota (58%)
Oct. 31 vs. Wisconsin (57%)
Nov. 7 at Northwestern (50%)

Putting it in those terms brings into focus how attainable a 5-1 or 6-0 finish could be for Iowa. The Hawkeyes won the division in 2015, 2021 and 2023 while competing against the six teams remaining on their schedule.
Revitalized Iowa offense
Iowa appears to have a quarterback controversy on its hands. Hecklinski completed 14 of 19 passes for 202 yards and three touchdowns in Friday night's win at Washington as the Hawkeyes racked up 465 total yards, including 279 in the first half. It was the first time since 2018 that the Hawkeyes produced 465 or more yards against a Big Ten opponent. Will Hecklinski keep the job once Brown is healthy?
The Hawkeyes have built their identity on a ruthless defense and elite special teams during the NIL era, but having an offense with a pulse makes Iowa a different type of challenge. Furthermore, the defense racked up six sacks and nine tackles for loss against Washington. This team's identity is a bit different than it has been in the past, but the defense remains potent.

Is the best team in the nation playing in Tuscaloosa, Alabama, this weekend?
It sure feels like the winner of No. 2 Georgia at No. 6 Alabamawill be able to make a strong claim to that designation after this weekend. Both teams are undefeated and in great position to return to the College Football Playoff this season.
Alabama leads the country in explosive plays and has the nation's No. 3 scoring offense, while Georgia ranks in the top 10 in rushing defense and scoring defense. It's strength-on-strength in a game that could be affected by weather as Hurricane Isaias makes its way up the state on Saturday.
Before Alabama and Georgia kick off Saturday night, you'll want to tune in to No. 21 UCLA at No. 13 Oregon (3:30 p.m. ET on CBS). The Bruins are riding high under first-year coach Bob Chesney and could be the 2024 version of Indiana if they can keep it going with a win over Oregon.
The Ducks have rebounded nicely since that early, shocking loss to Oklahoma State but are expected to be without quarterback Dante Moore against UCLA. A loss Saturday would be devastating to Oregon's CFP hopes -- the odds would drop to 19.6%, according to our CBS Sports forecasting and projections team.
Elsewhere in the Big Ten, undefeated No. 7 Indiana travels to undefeated Nebraska. Matt Rhule would love to end the Cornhuskers' ignominious 31-game losing streak against top-25 teams.
Could we get a trap game on Saturday? Other top-25 teams in potentially tricky matchups include No. 1 Texas vs. Oklahoma, No. 9 Ole Miss at Vanderbilt, No. 10 LSU at Kentucky, No. 14 Missouri at Texas A&M and No. 19 USC at Penn State.

Three of Oklahoma's four games against Texas under Venables cleared a 17-point margin of victory, and this Sooners squad might be the worst one yet. College football sometimes surprises you, but... this would be a surprise. Pick: Texas -8.5 -- Shehan Jeyarajah

Roman Wilson was already establishing himself as the No. 2 receiver in Pittsburgh behind DK Metcalf, and then Michael Pittman injured his foot in Week 4 and is expected to miss multiple weeks. Wilson is now in a great spot heading into Week 5 against the Colts, and he should be considered a sleeper in all leagues.
Wilson has six targets in every game this season, and he's hot coming into this matchup against Indianapolis. He has six catches for 134 yards and two touchdowns in his past two games against Cincinnati and Cleveland, and he has scored at least 15 PPR points in each outing.
The Colts have allowed four receivers to score at least 12.3 PPR points this season, and Metcalf and Wilson should be peppered with targets from Aaron Rodgers. I like Metcalf as a low-end No. 2 Fantasy receiver in all leagues in Week 5, and Wilson should be considered a high-end No. 3 receiver.
Wilson was only rostered in 57 percent of leagues on CBS Sports as of Friday afternoon, and he should be added in all formats. He could be a potential Fantasy starter over the next few weeks while Pittman is out.
